source: Migne's foot-of-page apparatus, read off raw/pg088/088.pdf at 600 dpi by the leaf transcribers (Sonnet) and adjudicated on the plate (Opus), 2026-08-07.

structure.note: ⛔ As throughout PG 88, every marker is printed in the LATIN column. No superscript appears anywhere in the Greek. The Greek chunks therefore carry NO [n:] markers — there is nothing in them to key one to. These notes attach to the ENGLISH at translation time.
structure.howToPlace: ⚑ THE NOTE'S OWN CITATION IS ITS LOCATOR. Migne prints the marker at the CLOSE OF THE SCRIPTURE QUOTATION the note names. Verified empirically 2026-08-07: of the eleven markers here, three survived the archive.org OCR of the Latin as `*`, and all three sit exactly at the end of the quotation they cite — `…sed ut convertatur et vivat *` (Ezech. xxxiii, 11), `…ad pœnitentiam *` (Matth. ix, 13), `…de crastino *` (Matth. vi, 34). So the translator places [n:] at the close of the quoted verse, using src/pg-latin/ to find where the quotation falls.
structure.whyNotMechanical: Only 3 of 11 markers survive in the OCR (3 on col 1842, 0 on col 1839). Superscripts are the first thing a scan layer loses, so marker POSITION cannot be harvested — it is read from the plate or inferred from the citation. Do not build a harvester that assumes otherwise.

columns.comment: None. The transcriber scanned the full column height on both sides of the title-block break.

notes.adjudicated: ⚠ The VERSE NUMBER was the transcriber's lowest-confidence reading (ink-damaged) and is now CONFIRMED 34 by pixel map: the stroke descends on the RIGHT after the top bar, which is this fount's flat-top 3. A 5 descends on the LEFT (cf. `n. 52` on leaf859). Settled structurally, NOT from Matthew having 34 verses. ⚑ Note that copyA's OCR of this same line reads `Ma th. vi, 54.` — the machine made exactly the error the plate reading rules out.
